Card Spending AbroadMonzo does not charge any fees for paying by card (or contactless/Apple Pay/Google Pay) in any currency abroad. They pass Mastercard's exchange rate directly onto you with no markup. (Tip: Always choose to pay in the local currency rather than GBP at card terminals or ATMs so you don't get hit by the merchant's own poor exchange rate.)   
Monzo
+ 1

Cash Withdrawals AbroadMonzo gives you a fee-free ATM allowance over a rolling 30-day period, after which they charge a 3% fee. Your allowance depends on where you are travelling and which Monzo account tier you have:   
Monzo

Account Type	UK & EEA*	Outside the EEA	Fee After Allowance
Free (Monzo is NOT your main bank)	£400 every 30 days	£200 every 30 days	3%
Free (Monzo IS your main bank)	Unlimited	£200 every 30 days	3%
Monzo Extra / legacy Plus	Unlimited	£200 (Extra) / £400 (Plus)	3%
Monzo Perks / Max / legacy Premium	Unlimited	£600 every 30 days	3%

*The EEA includes all EU countries plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway.   
Monzo

A few things to keep in mind:

Rolling 30-day reset: Your limit does not reset on the 1st of the month—each withdrawal drops off your allowance exactly 30 days after you made it.   
Monzo

"Main bank" criteria: Monzo generally counts as your main bank if you pay at least £500 into your account and have an active Direct Debit within a rolling 35-day period (or receive DWP/DfC benefit payments into it). You can check your exact live allowance in the app under Account > Fees and allowances.   
PocketWise
+ 1

Local ATM operator fees: Even when Monzo doesn't charge you, some overseas ATMs charge their own flat withdrawal fee (which will be shown on the ATM screen before you confirm).   
Monzo
